label: Vocal modes and audible events
description: Whispering, projection, laughter, and breath-catching. These are scored as actual vocal modes, not merely lower or higher volume.

styles.label: Whisper
styles.target_text: Keep your voice down. There is someone standing just outside the door.
styles.acted_reference_text: Do not turn around; the guard is close enough to hear us breathe.
styles.instruction: Whisper the entire line audibly with breathy low-volume phonation and close-mic urgency; do not merely speak softly.

styles.label: Shout
styles.target_text: Run! Get out of the building now!
styles.acted_reference_text: Stop the train! There is someone on the track!
styles.instruction: Shout with urgent projection and alarm. Be forceful and loud while preserving clear words and avoiding distortion.

styles.label: Laughing while speaking
styles.target_text: You should have seen his face when the harmless little box sprang open.
styles.acted_reference_text: The dog stole the hat again, and she could barely finish the story through her laughter.
styles.instruction: Speak with genuine audible laughter woven naturally into the line while keeping the words intelligible and avoiding canned giggling.

styles.label: Gasping / breath-catching
styles.target_text: There—behind the glass. I just saw someone move.
styles.acted_reference_text: The cold water struck his chest, and he fought to pull in a full breath.
styles.instruction: Begin with a natural gasp or sharply caught breath, then speak in startled breathlessness without losing intelligibility.
